title: What pushes a person into wrongdoing

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचअथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः । अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: O descendant of the Vrishni clan, what drives a person to commit wrongdoing, even unwillingly, as if forced?
verses.angle: bhavitavya: the word that shows Arjuna feels like a puppet
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna to do his own duty, so Arjuna pushes back, asking what power moves a person against their own will.

body.text: Arjuna says: O descendant of the Vrishni clan, what drives a person to commit wrongdoing, even unwillingly, as if forced? The word bhavitavya means appointed, and Arjuna uses it to describe himself. He is saying he feels like a puppet, driven by some outside force to do wrong, even though he does not want to. Krishna answers by naming desire as the force that drives a person into anger and destruction.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचकाम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः । महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥
verses.tr: Krishna says: Desire, born of rajas, turns into anger. It is all-consuming and deeply destructive. Know it as your enemy here.
verses.angle: kamah: the inner force that turns into anger
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna asked why a person commits sin even unwillingly. Krishna answers with one word: what is that force? Listen for it.

body.text: Krishna says: Desire, born of rajas, turns into anger. It is all-consuming and deeply destructive. Know it as your enemy here. Notice the word kamah, desire. The Lord presents it as the force that turns into krodha, anger, and warns Arjuna to recognize this single enemy within himself. Krishna then shows how this desire covers clear seeing like smoke covers a fire.

verses.sa: धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च । यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥
verses.tr: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and a womb by a membrane, so clear seeing is covered by desire.
verses.angle: Three pairs of covering and object
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna compares the way desire hides wisdom to three everyday coverings. Listen for how the third object is paired with its cover.

body.text: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and a womb by a membrane, so clear seeing is covered by desire. The verse lists three objects that are covered, and the word avrtam, covered, appears twice. The first covering is smoke over fire, the second is dust on a mirror, and the third is a membrane over a womb. Krishna moves from the covering to the covering agent, calling desire the eternal enemy of the wise.

verses.sa: आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा । कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥
verses.tr: O son of Kunti, wisdom is covered by this desire, the eternal enemy of the wise, as fire is never satisfied.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to one force that hides wisdom. Listen for the image of a fire that never says enough.

body.text: O son of Kunti, wisdom is covered by this desire, the eternal enemy of the wise, as fire is never satisfied. Krishna names desire the eternal enemy of the wise. He calls it a fire that can never be satisfied. He then shows exactly where this fire lives, inside the senses and the mind.

verses.sa: इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते । एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ॥
verses.tr: The senses, the mind, and the discerning mind are said to be its seat. Through them, it deludes the embodied person by veiling understanding.
verses.angle: The seat of desire is inside the mind
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is tracing the enemy inside the human system. Listen to the exact instruments desire uses to cloud a person's judgment.

body.text: The senses, the mind, and the discerning mind are said to be its seat. Through them, it deludes the embodied person by veiling understanding. Krishna names three instruments, the senses, the mind, and the discerning mind, as the seat of desire. All three together form the base through which knowledge is veiled and the embodied person is deluded. Krishna now tells Arjuna to first control the senses and then destroy this great sinner.

verses.sa: तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ । पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥
verses.tr: Therefore, O best of the Bharatas, first control the senses, and then destroy this great sinner, the destroyer of knowledge and wisdom.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described desire as the force that blinds judgment from within. Now he gives the first practical step to fight it.

body.text: Therefore, O best of the Bharatas, first control the senses, and then destroy this great sinner, the destroyer of knowledge and wisdom. Notice the word adau, first. Krishna does not ask Arjuna to strike down desire immediately. He sets a clear order. First restrain the senses, because they are the gateway through which desire enters and clouds judgment. Senses are only the first line of defense, for the mind and the discerning mind sit even higher.

verses.sa: इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः । मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥
verses.tr: The senses are higher than the body; the mind is higher than the senses; the discerning mind is higher than the mind. And beyond the discerning mind is the self.
verses.angle: A ladder of higher and higher layers
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks which enemy is hardest to conquer, and answers by mapping the inner layers. Listen for the ladder that leads upward.

body.text: The senses are higher than the body; the mind is higher than the senses; the discerning mind is higher than the mind. And beyond the discerning mind is the self. The word parah means higher than the one below, and Krishna builds a ladder with it. The senses are higher than the body, the mind is higher than the senses, the discerning mind is higher than the mind, and the self is higher than the discerning mind. Krishna now tells Arjuna to use this knowledge to steady the self and destroy desire.

verses.sa: एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना । जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥
verses.tr: Thus, knowing the higher beyond the intellect, steady the lower self by the higher self, and destroy that enemy in the form of desire, which is hard to conquer.
verses.angle: Steadying the self with the Self
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna maps the inner battlefield from senses to mind to intellect. Listen for the moment he names the real enemy.

body.text: Thus, knowing the higher beyond the intellect, steady the lower self by the higher self, and destroy that enemy in the form of desire, which is hard to conquer. Krishna commands Arjuna to steady the lower self, atmanam, with the higher self, atmana. The battle is not won by fighting the senses but by letting the deeper self hold the reins. Krishna now turns to the lineage of this teaching, passing the imperishable knowledge down from Vivasvan to Manu.
